description:

Through partnership and collaborations, we work to ensure the inclusion of older people across society and strive to deliver a just and fair world for everyone as they get older. Our work is driven by our desire to achieve real impact for older people, to be inclusive, to work in partnership and to learn from our shared experience. About the Job The Head of Advocacy & Evidencing provides strategic leadership and organisational accountability for HelpAge’s global advocacy, policy and research agendas, ensuring that external engagement is grounded in rigorous evidence, shaped by the lived experiences of older people, and aligned with organisational priorities. Key areas for impact/influence and responsibilities To deliver impact, the Head of Advocacy & Evidencing will: Lead the delivery and evolution of HelpAge’s global advocacy and research agenda, ensuring it reflects lived experience and drives progress on rights, inclusion, and equity for older people. Strengthen the capacities of network members and older people to lead and participate meaningfully in advocacy efforts, and ensure inclusive engagement in the design and implementation of influencing strategies. Cultivate strategic partnerships with policy, academic, and research institutions to co-produce high-quality, policy-relevant evidence and promote HelpAge’s thought leadership on rights, healthy ageing, humanitarian inclusion, and social protection. Key Responsibilities Strategic Leadership and Advocacy Lead and be accountable for the development, implementation and results of HelpAge’s global advocacy and evidencing strategy, aligned with HelpAge’s impact areas and co-created with network members. Monitor and respond to global, regional and national policy trends,advising colleagues and network members on opportunities for engagement and influence. Champion inclusive, partner-led advocacy approaches that centre the voices and leadership of older people and civil society actors. Collaborate with the Fundraising and Strategic Partnerships Director and supporting members to align donor advocacy efforts with organisational priorities and global influencing strategies. Advise the Executive Leadership Group and the Board on HelpAge's advocacy positions and external positioning, and lead the preparation and quality of the related papers and briefings. Where appropriate, represent HelpAge's positions externally alongside senior leaders. Lead and coordinate HelpAge's influencing in priority global and regional policy and donor markets, including Europe, identifying opportunities to position ageing and the rights of older people within relevant policy, development and humanitarian agendas and, in collaboration with Fundraising, strengthen HelpAge's positioning with institutional donors and partners. Be accountable for achieving the agreed Advocacy & Evidencing income target. Working in partnership with the Fundraising & Strategic Partnerships team, play a lead technical and relationship role in shaping fundable propositions, contributing to pipeline development, and donor cultivation and stewardship for advocacy and research. Ensure that advocacy, research and evidence-generation activities comply with HelpAge’s ethical, safeguarding, data protection and relevant organisational standards, and hold team members accountable for compliance within their areas of responsibility. Represent HelpAge at senior level in key global and regional coalitions, alliances and policy forums, proactively building strategic relationships with governments, multilateral and donor institutions, policy actors and other influential stakeholders to advance HelpAge’s advocacy priorities and strengthen its external positioning. Evidence and Research Lead and be accountable for HelpAge’s global research and evidence agenda, ensuring that it is coherent, ethical, inclusive and aligned with organisational advocacy and programme priorities. Provide strategic oversight of HelpAge’s global portfolio of evidence generation, policy analysis and advocacy initiatives across key impact areas, ensuring coherence, quality and alignment with organisational strategy and drawing on the network as a central source of evidence and insight. Foster partnerships with academic institutions, think tanks, and research bodies to co-produce and validate robust, policy-influencing evidence. Ensure that research outputs are accessible, actionable, and designed for strategic influence at global and national levels. Capacity Strengthening and Network Engagement Lead on advocacy capacity strengthening of HelpAge network members and older people through mentoring, training, and tailored support. Promote knowledge exchange and peer learning across the global network, ensuring inclusive participation in advocacy platforms and decision-making spaces. Collaborate with regional colleagues to support the development and implementation of national and regional advocacy strategies led by network members. Team and Resource Management Lead, manage, and coach a multidisciplinary team of advocacy advisers, ensuring high performance and alignment with organisational goals. These are hybrid roles, with approximately 50% of their time dedicated to global advocacy and the remaining 50% focused on technical support to network members and contribution to programme development. Manage advocacy and research budgets effectively, ensuring compliance with donor requirements and strategic resource allocation. Cross-Organisational Collaboration Work closely with Programme Support, Network Development, MEAL, Fundraising, and Communications teams to embed evidence and influencing in all areas of work. Coordinate joint advocacy and research initiatives that connect policy engagement with programme delivery and impact measurement. Skills and experience required Essential Proven strategic leadership in global advocacy, policy influencing, and research within the international development, humanitarian, or human rights sectors. Strong leadership, planning, and performance management skills, with a track record of delivering results through high-performing, diverse, and remote multidisciplinary teams. Deep understanding and practical application of rights-based, inclusive, and intersectional approaches—especially relating to age, gender, disability, and displacement. Demonstrated success in designing and implementing partner-led advocacy strategies that centre lived experience and community priorities. Experience influencing policy at national, regional and international levels through coalition-building and senior-level relationships with governments, multilateral bodies and donors. Strong analytical and research skills, with experience designing or overseeing ethical, participatory research and translating evidence into compelling policy and advocacy outputs. Demonstrated ability to build and sustain high-impact partnerships with academic institutions, think tanks and policy platforms. Track record of securing income for advocacy or research, including developing fundable propositions and engaging institutional donors with fundraising colleagues. Skilled in budget oversight and resource management, including accountability in donor-funded initiatives. Ability to monitor advocacy impact, policy trends, and funding landscapes, and to adapt strategies accordingly. Experience of strengthening the capacity of civil society, networks or grassroots movements, particularly in low- and middle-income countries, through mentoring, training and tailored support. Lived experience of the Global South or extensive professional experience working in Global South contexts. Desirable Strong knowledge and networks in European/global institutional policy and donor environments Experience engaging with media to support advocacy. Education and Qualifications Degree in international development, public policy, human rights, social sciences, or a related field (or equivalent professional experience). A postgraduate qualification is an asset but not essential where practical experience is strong. Other Requirements Willingness to travel internationally Ability to work across cultures, sectors, and geographies in inclusive and equitable ways. Excellent communication skills in English (spoken and written); additional languages used in the Global South (e.g., Spanish, French, Arabic) are highly desirable. Deep commitment to locally led development and the principles of Partner-Led Programming. We actively value and encourage candidates with lived experience of inequality, marginalisation, or systemic exclusion—especially related to age, gender, disability, displacement, or economic injustice. Familiarity with ageing, inclusion, and rights issues in Global South contexts is a key asset. Adaptability and Flexibility: Adapt to new directions or opportunities arising within the organisation and in our work area; being flexible in our role, constantly using the feedback to learn more and evolve further. Supporting and Facilitating Change: Lead behavioural and cultural change through embracing a supportive, collaborative and highly inclusive environment where everybody feels supported, respected and engaged. Extend HelpAge’s Reach and Impact: Extend HelpAge’s reach and impact by creating and identifying new business development opportunities and building relationships with new partners. Diversity and Inclusion: Lead and promote a culture of including the voices of older people across our support, convening and thought leadership roles, in a way that is transformative, empowering and highly inclusive of those marginalised by gender, economic status, disability and other factors of discrimination. Leading Others (for managers): Demonstrate strong leadership to own unit/department and manage people in a well and reputable manner. Create an atmosphere of trust and an enabling environment where staff can contribute their best and develop their potential. Safeguarding HelpAge International is committed to safeguarding the communities with which we work, our partners, staff and any others who we come into contact with. The post holder will also be responsible for: Preventing harm and abuse from our people, operations and programmes to anyone that encounters our work. Reporting all safeguarding incidents you see, hear, hear about or suspect, using our internal reporting mechanism. Complying with all safeguarding framework policies and practices. title: ETHIOPIA - FIELD COORDINATOR (M/F) - TIGRAY
description:
Desired start date: 01/12/2026 Duration of the mission: 6 Months Location: Adwa - Tigray Region SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI) is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms. PRESENTATION OF THE MISSION: Solidarités International (SI) was registered in Ethiopia in December 2022, having previously implemented a WASH in Health intervention in Jijiga, Somali Region, in 2017. In November 2023, SI became the first humanitarian actor to operate in Mao Komo Special woreda (Benishangul-Gumuz) by rehabilitating water points in areas that had been inaccessible for three years. Currently, SI is operational in two regions of the country (In Tigray Region and Amhara Region). In Tigray, bordering Eritrea, focusing on hard-to-reach areas in partnership with Mums for Mums (MfM) SI is implementing an emergency multisectoral humanitarian programme in Ahsea and Rama Woredas of central zone, to support communities affected by drought, conflict, and displacement. Running from September 2024 to December 2025 (which is now to be extended until end of June 2026), the project aims to improve access to safe water, health services, and nutrition support, while addressing gender-based violence and mental health needs. Key activities include rehabilitating water systems and health facilities, community-based malnutrition screening, cash assistance for vulnerable households, and capacity-building for local actors. In Amhara region, Solidarités International (SI) and Première Urgence Internationale (PUI) are jointly implementing an integrated emergency response program in the Amhara region of Ethiopia, primarily focused on Health and Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) services. This program is part of a wider effort to address the significant humanitarian needs in the region caused by ongoing conflict and displacement. SI has been granted cost extension (the donor contract is extended until end of June 2026 with additional fund allocation) of existing project in Tigray and is looking for a Field Coordinator to continue the project activities in the same area. GENERAL OBJECTIVES : The Field Coordinator is the representative of the organization at field level. He/she proposes a strategy for his/her area, according to the geopolitical and humanitarian context, and ensures its implementation once validated. He/she checks and ensures that projects are carried out in accordance with the Solidarités International charter, respecting all internal and contractual procedures. He/she mobilizes the material and financial resources necessary for programs to run smoothly and supervises resource management. He/she coordinates the teams in place and is responsible for their security in his/her assigned zone. Representation and Internal / external communication: The FC is the official representative of Solidarités International in his/her intervention zone for NGOs, administrative, political and local authorities and civil society. He/She participates in humanitarian forums and relevant coordination meetings The FC Ensure that documents produced in his/her intervention zone meet deadlines and quality standards, respecting standard formats and procedures The FC Organise regular Base meetings and Ensure that key operational information circulates properly, in his/her intervention zone and between the bases and the country coordination (sitrep). ISSUES AND SPECIFIC CHALLENGES : Implement activities across several woredas in a volatile and operationally constrained context, while ensuring quality, compliance and timely delivery of ongoing projects. Maintain access and programme continuity despite recurrent constraints linked to fuel availability, cash liquidity, telecommunications/network coverage, road access and market fluctuations. Maintain adequate preparedness for a potential deterioration of the security situation, including possible disruption of banking services, communications and movements. PRIORITIES ON THE 2-3 FIRST MONTHS : -Consolidate the base management structure and ensure clear responsibilities, delegation and reporting lines within Programme and Support teams. -Ensure timely implementation and close monitoring of ongoing activities through updated workplans, APU/OFU/LFU and procurement plans. -Strengthen coordination between WASH, Livelihoods, MEAL and Support departments and ensure adequate balance of management capacity between the main programme components. -Reinforce budget forecasting and absorption monitoring. -Maintain and strengthen coordination with local authorities, clusters, partners and other humanitarian actors to avoid duplication and identify operational synergies. -Ensure the base is prepared for emergency scenarios through updated contingency plans, communication systems, cash/fuel contingency measures and staff preparedness, especially this year with the evolving context -Continue effort of base development with upcoming opportunities SECURITY CONSTRAINTS : The security environment in Tigray remains potentially volatile and can evolve rapidly, requiring continuous monitoring and strict compliance with SI security procedures. Main operational constraints include possible access restrictions, interruptions to telecommunications and internet, fuel shortages, banking/cash limitations and disruptions to road movements. Some operational areas may have limited or no network coverage, requiring reinforced movement tracking and communication procedures. The Field Coordinator must maintain a high level of preparedness, regularly review contingency arrangements, ensure critical resources are available, and adapt programme implementation and movements according to changes in the security and access environment. Staff safety and duty of care must remain central to operational decision-making. YOUR PROFIL : DIPLOMAS : A master’s degree (or equivalent field experience) in Humanitarian Action, International Development, Social Sciences, Project Management, or a related field is required. EXPERIMENT IN THE HUMANITARIAN SECTOR : more than 5 years EXPERIMENT ON SIMILAR POSITIONS : 3-4 years TECHNICAL SKILLS : Relevant management skills :Operation and team management skills include leadership, communication, and problem-solving as core competencies. Other essential skills are decision-making, time management, adaptability, and organizational abilities. Including a strong understanding of finance, and logistics processes. TRANSVERSAL SKILLS : Ability to work under pressure in a challenging and sometimes insecure environment; cultural sensitivity, adaptability, and a strong commitment to humanitarian principles and safeguarding policies (PSEA, Child Protection). LANGUAGES : Fluency in written and spoken English is essential. Knowledge of the local language(s) (e.g., Amharic, Tigrigna) is a strong asset. SI WILL OFFER YOU : A salaried position: According to experience, starting from EUR 3080 gross per month (2800 base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 400. SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment. Breaks: During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every three months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked. Insurance package: Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded. Living conditions: Guest House conditions : - There will be shared guesthouse both at the project and coordination during the visit. -Internet and telephone network : Available both in Addis and Adwa -Restaurant & social life: Restaurants are available in Addis and also Adwa : - Social life in Adwa is limited. All the basics food items and other are available but there is strict limitations and taxation to importation of food. Food in your luggage however is allowed and you can stock up on specials from home. Good quality chocolate, cereals and dried meat products can be hard to find and/or very expensive.

title: Request For Proposal Field Research Services for the Yegna Gize Impact Study Ethiopia October 2026
description:
Request For Proposal Field Research Services for the Yegna Gize Impact Study Ethiopia October 2026 Procurement Summary Item Details RFP title Field Research Services for the Yegna Gize Impact Study Supplier type Research or data-collection agency Contract type Framework/on-call arrangement using task orders Geographic scope Tigray, Amhara, Oromia, Sidama, Central Ethiopia and South Ethiopia Anticipated contract period October 2026 to September 2027 RFP issue date 5 October 2026 Proposal deadline 12 October 2026 Submission email suppliers@girleffect.org Proposal validity 90 days Who We Are Girl Effect is an international non-profit organization dedicated to addressing challenges faced by adolescent girls and youth in Ethiopia. Operating in the country since 2013, the organization leverages Social and Behavior Change (SBC) strategies, combining media and on-the-ground interventions to tackle various societal issues and empower young people. Girl Effect Ethiopia created the youth brand Yegna in 2014 and, since then, has reached over 10 million people through multiple products, outreach programs, girl networks, and research pieces done all for the betterment of adolescent lives. We create safe spaces for girls, sharing facts and answering questions about health, nutrition, education, relationships, etc. And we use innovative technology so we can reach girls at scale. We arm girls with the skills to negotiate and redefine what they are told is possible, so every girl can choose to be in control of her body, her health, her learning and livelihood. When a girl unlocks her power to make different choices that change her life, it inspires others to do so too. She starts a ripple effect that impacts her family, community, and country. That’s the Girl Effect. Background Yegna Gize, meaning “Our Time” in Amharic, is a Girl Effect Ethiopia programme that builds on the Yegna brand and its experience of using media, storytelling, role modelling, and community engagement to influence positive social and behavioural change among young people. Yegna Gize focuses specifically on youth economic empowerment, with an emphasis on improving young people's aspirations, mindsets, skills, access to opportunities, and pathways towards employment and entrepreneurship. Over the programme period, Yegna Gize seeks to contribute to improved economic opportunities and livelihood outcomes for young people in Ethiopia by addressing barriers related to employment, entrepreneurship, skills development, social norms, and mindsets. The programme works with young people, schools, communities, government institutions, civil society organisations (CSOs), private-sector actors, role models, and other relevant stakeholders to create an enabling environment for youth to pursue viable economic pathways. The programme is implemented across six regions of Ethiopia: Tigray, Oromia, Amhara, Central Ethiopia, Sidama, and South Ethiopia. Through a combination of youth-centred interventions, partnerships, capacity strengthening, communication and social and behavioural change approaches, Yegna Gize aims to strengthen young people's knowledge, skills, confidence, aspirations, networks, and access to employment and entrepreneurship opportunities. Key areas of Yegna Gize programming include: Youth employment and transition to work: Supporting young people to access internships, work-based learning, employment opportunities, and other pathways into the labour market. Entrepreneurship and enterprise development: Strengthening entrepreneurial knowledge, business skills, growth mindsets, and access to support for young people interested in starting or growing businesses. Skills and mindset development: Building practical, transferable, entrepreneurial, and employability skills, alongside confidence, aspirations, resilience, and positive attitudes towards work and entrepreneurship. Peer-to-peer and youth support mechanisms: Establishing and strengthening youth groups and peer-support approaches that enable young people to learn from and support one another. Role modelling and mentorship: Connecting young people with role models, mentors, entrepreneurs, and other influential individuals who can provide inspiration, guidance, and practical exposure to different livelihood pathways. School-based engagement: Working with schools, teachers, students, and relevant stakeholders to promote entrepreneurship, creativity, growth mindset, career aspirations, and awareness of economic opportunities. Youth-centred media and social and behavioural change communication (SBC): Using Yegna's established multimedia and storytelling platforms to challenge limiting norms, promote positive attitudes towards work and entrepreneurship, and increase young people's awareness and uptake of available opportunities. Partnerships and systems strengthening: Working with regional and local government structures, CSOs, private-sector actors, educational institutions, and other stakeholders to strengthen the ecosystem supporting youth economic empowerment. Girl Effect works with local partners to contextualise and implement interventions according to regional realities and the needs of young people. The programme therefore combines national-level approaches with locally relevant implementation, allowing interventions to respond to the different economic, social, cultural, and institutional contexts across the six regions. Yegna Gize Programme Impact Study As the programme progresses, Girl Effect Ethiopia intends to commission an independent Impact Study of Yegna Gize to assess the extent to which the programme has contributed to changes in young people's knowledge, skills, attitudes, aspirations, behaviours, access to opportunities, and economic outcomes. The study is expected to generate credible evidence on the effectiveness, relevance, and contribution of Yegna Gize interventions and to identify which approaches are working, for whom, under what conditions, and why. The findings will inform programme learning, adaptation, accountability to stakeholders and donors, and future programming and scale-up decisions. The selected agency will therefore be expected to develop and implement a rigorous and contextually appropriate study methodology that captures both quantitative and qualitative evidence, where appropriate, and considers the diversity of young people, intervention types, implementation approaches, and regional contexts within Yegna Gize. The study should generate actionable evidence and recommendations that can strengthen the programme's contribution to sustainable youth economic empowerment in Ethiopia. title: RESPONSABLE DU BUREAU DE PLAIDOYER ET DE LIAISON AUPRÈS DE L’UNION AFRICAINE, Oxfam en Afrique
description:
Type de contrat : Contrat à durée déterminée de 2 ans Grade interne : B1, International Rémunération : conforme à la grille salariale d’Oxfam International. Cette offre comprend les avantages sociaux de base ainsi que les prestations globales applicables au personnel recruté à l’international et relocalisé.Nous considérons que les modalités de travail flexibles sont essentielles pour bâtir le Secrétariat de demain. Nous sommes donc disposés à échanger avec vous sur les modalités susceptibles de vous convenir. Le poste Oxfam en Afrique recherche une personne expérimentée, dotée d’un leadership reconnu et d’un forte capacité d’influence, pour diriger son Bureau de plaidoyer et de liaison auprès de l’Union africaine (UA), basé à Addis-Abeba. En tant que membre de l’Équipe de direction de la Plateforme Afrique, vous piloterez l’engagement d’Oxfam auprès de l’Union africaine et de ses institutions. Vous élaborerez et mettrez en œuvre des stratégies de plaidoyer à fort impact afin d’influencer les politiques et les pratiques à l’échelle continentale. Vous représenterez Oxfam au plus haut niveau auprès de l’UA, nouerez des relations stratégiques et contribuerez à positionner Oxfam comme un partenaire crédible et de confiance. Ce poste joue un rôle central dans la réalisation de la mission d’Oxfam en Afrique : il établit un lien entre les espaces d’élaboration des politiques continentales et les réalités nationales, tout en veillant à ce que les actions de plaidoyer soient cohérentes, porteuses d’impact et ancrées dans les réalités vécues par les communautés. Ce poste relève de la Direction Afrique, avec un rattachement matriciel à la Direction Plaidoyer, Campagnes et Engagement (ACE). Profil recherché Nous recherchons une personne reconnue pour son leadership en matière de plaidoyer et d’influence, disposant d’une solide expérience de collaboration avec l’Union africaine ou des institutions multilatérales comparables. Vous avez démontré votre capacité à concevoir et à mettre en œuvre des stratégies d’influence porteuses d’impact, combinant analyse des politiques, plaidoyer, communication médiatique et partenariats afin de favoriser des changements significatifs. Vous excellez dans l’établissement de relations et la négociation, savez évoluer efficacement dans des environnements complexes associant de multiples parties prenantes et êtes en mesure d’exercer une influence au plus haut niveau. Grâce à votre capacité de réflexion stratégique et d’analyse politique, vous savez traduire les processus de l’UA en possibilités concrètes d’influence et d’impact pour les pays et les partenaires. Votre expérience du leadership vous permet de diriger des équipes diversifiées et de travailler au sein d’un réseau mondial, tout en favorisant la collaboration et la redevabilité. Vous avez une connaissance approfondie du contexte sociopolitique africain et adhérez aux approches féministes, décoloniales et portées par les partenaires. La maîtrise professionnelle de l’anglais et du français est indispensable. Pourquoi nous rejoindre Ce poste offre une occasion rare d’influencer les politiques et les pratiques au plus haut niveau continental. À Oxfam, vous façonnerez notre engagement auprès de l’Union africaine, piloterez le plaidoyer sur des enjeux majeurs tels que les inégalités, la pauvreté et la justice, et collaborerez avec des gouvernements, des diplomates et des institutions internationales pour réaliser des changements concrets. Au sein d’une équipe de direction diversifiée et collaborative, vous contribuerez à rapprocher les politiques continentales des réalités des communautés, afin que les décisions prises au plus haut niveau se traduisent par des résultats tangibles pour les populations partout en Afrique. Ce que nous offrons À Oxfam, nous sommes convaincus que chaque aspect de notre travail peut contribuer à un changement positif. Si vous partagez cette conviction et possédez les compétences nécessaires pour relever les défis liés à ce poste, cette fonction vous offrira de grandes possibilités d’épanouissement personnel ainsi que d’excellentes perspectives d’évolution professionnelle. Oxfam s’engage à proposer une rémunération équitable, sur la base d’une semaine de travail de 36 heures À propos de nous Oxfam est un mouvement mondial de personnes qui agissent ensemble pour mettre fin à l’injustice qu’est la pauvreté. Cela signifie que nous nous attaquons aux inégalités qui maintiennent les populations dans la pauvreté. Ensemble, nous sauvons des vies, protégeons les populations et les aidons à reconstruire leur existence. Lorsqu’une catastrophe survient, nous aidons les personnes à bâtir un avenir meilleur, pour elles-mêmes et pour les autres. Nous agissons sur des enjeux tels que les droits fonciers, le changement climatique et les discriminations à l’égard des femmes. Et nous ne nous arrêterons pas tant que chaque personne sur la planète ne pourra pas vivre à l’abri de la pauvreté. Nous sommes une confédération internationale composée de 22 organisations affiliées et du Secrétariat d’Oxfam International. Avec nos partenaires et les communautés locales, nous menons des actions humanitaires, des programmes de développement et des campagnes dans plus de 76 pays. title: Physiotherapist
description:
The Physiotherapist is responsible for the treatment, counselling, preventative care and rehabilitation of the motor function and physical wellness of the patients. is responsible for assessing, planning, implementing, and evaluating individualized rehabilitation programs for patients with limb loss and other mobility impairments. Working within a multidisciplinary team, the Physiotherapist facilitates functional recovery, promotes independence, optimizes prosthetic use, and improves patients’ quality of life through evidence-based rehabilitation practices The Physiotherapist tasks and responsibilities include, but are not limited to, the following points: Undertake a comprehensive and accurate assessment of patients in a variety of settings; Identify, plan and manage physiotherapy interventions and rehabilitation plans Provide physio treatments to achieve identified outcomes and monitor patients’ conditions, both for in-patients and out-patients, if needed; Perform all the tasks related to the physio competence framework; Establish, maintain and conclude therapeutic interpersonal relationships with patients and their relatives, based on respect, dignity and care; Conduct comprehensive physical assessments of patients with upper and lower limb amputations, including musculoskeletal, neurological, cardiovascular, balance, gait, and functional evaluations. Provide pre-prosthetic rehabilitation, including: residual limb care and shaping, edema management, scar management, pain management (including phantom limb pain where appropriate), range of motion and strengthening exercises, contracture prevention Cardiovascular conditioning Deliver prosthetic rehabilitation, including: prosthetic gait training, balance and coordination training, functional mobility training Stair negotiation and community ambulation Transfers and activities of daily living (ADL) training Fall prevention strategies Monitor patient progress and modify treatment plans according to clinical outcomes. Encourage patients to have a positive attitude towards physiotherapy by motivating them; Organizing daily group activities, if possible, for patients; Promote an environment that enables patient’s safety and health implementing all necessary actions such as infection control practices, bed sores prevention practices and maintaining high level of hygiene also ensuring physio material are properly cleaned; Ensure that the equipment is functional and well maintained and stored; Ensure documentation/record is accurate and physio chart is properly filled, maintaining confidentially of information; Compiling and submitting periodic reports, if requested, following EMERGENCY guidelines; Be compliant with EMERGENCY guidelines for the treatment of patients; Work closely with prosthetists/orthotists during prosthetic prescription, fitting, alignment, and follow-up. Provide clinical feedback regarding prosthetic fit, function, comfort, and patient performance. Participate in training programs or activities, meeting timelines and deliverables, if requested by EMERGENCY; Train new staff, if needed. Job requirements: Degree in the Physio field; (Bachelor’s Degree in Physiotherapy from a recognized institution). Postgraduate training in rehabilitation, prosthetics, amputee rehabilitation, or neurorehabilitation Experience working in prosthetic and orthotic services. Good problem solving, time management and technical skills and willingness to learn new procedures and techniques; Good communication, interpersonal skills and high level of empathy, patience and ability to handle emotional and pressure situations; Basic Computer Skills, including Microsoft Office Program; Good level of English, written and spoken.

Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our Why Work Here blog post. In Ethiopia, we engage farmers in agroforestry and community-based seed multiplication to increase farmers’ incomes and make farming systems more resilient. PIN empowers civil society, advocates for human rights, and promotes social inclusion both at home and abroad. PIN is present in Ethiopia since 2003, works in partnership with communities, local organisations and public institutions to support sustainable development and improve people’s well-being across the country. Through integrated programming, PIN combines immediate assistance with longer-term, systems-oriented approaches aimed at strengthening resilience, expanding access to essential services and economic opportunities, and enabling locally led solutions. About the role: The Economic Programming and Private Business Partnerships Advisor will play a central role in shaping and strengthening People in Need Ethiopia’s economic and private business programming portfolio. Our programs strengthen public health systems and address the world’s leading causes of illness, injury and death. We currently work in 73 countries, supporting data-driven decision making in government, advancing evidence-based public health policies, and mounting strategic communication campaigns. Vital Strategies’ priorities are driven by the greatest potential to improve and save lives. They include non-communicable disease prevention, tobacco control, road safety, obesity prevention, overdose prevention, environmental health, and vital statistics systems building. Our programs are primarily concentrated in low- and middle-income countries in Africa, Latin America, Asia and the Pacific. Please visit our website at www.vitalstrategies.org to find out more about our work. Vital Strategies is committed to building a diverse, equitable and inclusive (DEI) organization. We believe our programs are strengthened when they are developed and supported by individuals with diverse life experiences, whose understanding of social and cultural issues can help make our work and workforce more inclusive. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds. Lead Poisoning Prevention Program: Vital Strategies is expanding our program that addresses the issue of lead poisoning in low- and middle-income countries. We plan to build upon existing efforts and interest by collaborating with governmental agencies in countries in Africa, Asia, and Latin America to strengthen health systems and build local expertise in childhood lead exposure to enact sound, cost-effective policies to address exposures. Job Purpose: The position of Government Relations Advisor, Africa will facilitate regional exchange and coordinate high-level engagement and partnership building for the Lead Poisoning Prevention Program across multiple countries in Africa. The role will focus on managing and strengthening relationships with key government and program partners, stakeholders, facilitating regional exchanges and strategy development, and ensuring program alignment with countries’ priorities and global objectives. The incumbent will work closely with country teams to support government engagement, partnership building, share updates on implementation progress, and ensure exchange and coordination among government and consortium partners across the regional portfolio. The role will also provide representation at regional events, support policy engagement, and ensure effective collaboration among regional stakeholders and technical partners. It is preferred that this role be based in Ethiopia, on a full-time hybrid schedule, out of Vital Strategies' office in Addis Ababa, but we are also open to qualified candidates from Ghana, Rwanda, and Tanzania. Partnership Management - · Support country teams in managing key government and institutional partners across the region, as well as non-government organizations in relevant sectors; · Represent Vital Strategies in regional lead poisoning prevention meetings, technical forums, public hearings, and governance bodies in the region; · Support the development and review of reports, policy briefs, and training materials developed in the region; · Promote cross-sector dialogues that support the development of integrated, evidence-based public policies; · Facilitate knowledge exchange across the region; · Coordinate work with national and international partners, ensuring alignment across local and global strategies; · Assist with other duties as specified by the supervisor. Qualifications: Education & Degree - · Master’s degree in public health, public policy/Administration, Global Health, international development, environmental health science, or related field. Skills & Abilities - · Strong government engagement and partnership-building skills, with the ability to establish and sustain relationships with ministries, regulatory bodies, and regional institutions; · Demonstrated ability to coordinate multi-country initiatives and facilitate regional exchange and collaboration; · Strategic thinking skills, with the ability to translate regional strategy into actionable country-level implementation plans; · Strong stakeholder management skills across government, NGOs, multilateral agencies, and technical partners; · Ability to promote and facilitate multisectoral collaboration and policy dialogue; · Ability to monitor program quality, performance, and outcomes across a regional portfolio; · Ability to coordinate and engage program stakeholders and other country teams; · Demonstrated sensitivity in handling confidential information; · Proven ability to interpret public health data, generate actionable insights, and support policy recommendations; · Exhibits strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple competing priorities and meet deadlines; demonstrates personal integrity, credibility, and professionalism while taking initiative and making sound, informed decisions in a fast-paced environment; · Professional oral and written proficiency in English; · Excellent interpersonal skills, including the ability to communicate effectively to technical and non-technical audiences, and contribute to an interdisciplinary international team; · Solid knowledge of Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Outlook); · Experience working with a geographically distributed team with demonstrated ability to work collaboratively, communicate clearly and regularly, monitor performance, and inspire, engage, and motivate staff; · Demonstrated commitment to contributing to an inclusive working and learning environment. Preferred - · Demonstrated experience in communicating scientific and health information to varied audiences; · Experience in using project management platforms. Working Conditions and Physical Requirements: · If hired in Ghana, Rwanda, or Tanzania, the candidate will be hired via Vital Strategies’ Employer of Record on a remote schedule; · The position will require travel up to 30% of the time to visit operating countries in the region to visit field implementation or attend meetings with partners; · The candidate needs to be willing to work with colleagues across different time zones.

title: Request For Proposal Field Research Services for the Yegna Gize Impact Study
description:
Who We Are

Girl Effect is an international non-profit organization dedicated to addressing challenges faced by adolescent girls and youth in Ethiopia. Operating in the country since 2013, the organization leverages Social and Behavior Change (SBC) strategies, combining media and on-the-ground interventions to tackle various societal issues and empower young people. Girl Effect Ethiopia created the youth brand Yegna in 2014 and, since then, has reached over 10 million people through multiple products, outreach programs, girl networks, and research pieces done all for the betterment of adolescent lives.

We create safe spaces for girls, sharing facts and answering questions about health, nutrition, education, relationships, etc. And we use innovative technology so we can reach girls at scale. We arm girls with the skills to negotiate and redefine what they are told is possible, so every girl can choose to be in control of her body, her health, her learning and livelihood.

When a girl unlocks her power to make different choices that change her life, it inspires others to do so too. She starts a ripple effect that impacts her family, community, and country. 

That’s the Girl Effect.

Background

Yegna Gize, meaning “Our Time” in Amharic, is a Girl Effect Ethiopia programme that builds on the Yegna brand and its experience of using media, storytelling, role modelling, and community engagement to influence positive social and behavioural change among young people. Yegna Gize focuses specifically on youth economic empowerment, with an emphasis on improving young peoples aspirations, mindsets, skills, access to opportunities, and pathways towards employment and entrepreneurship.

Over the programme period, Yegna Gize seeks to contribute to improved economic opportunities and livelihood outcomes for young people in Ethiopia by addressing barriers related to employment, entrepreneurship, skills development, social norms, and mindsets. The programme works with young people, schools, communities, government institutions, civil society organisations (CSOs), private-sector actors, role models, and other relevant stakeholders to create an enabling environment for youth to pursue viable economic pathways.

The programme is implemented across six regions of Ethiopia: Tigray, Oromia, Amhara, Central Ethiopia, Sidama, and South Ethiopia. Through a combination of youth-centred interventions, partnerships, capacity strengthening, communication and social and behavioural change approaches, Yegna Gize aims to strengthen young peoples knowledge, skills, confidence, aspirations, networks, and access to employment and entrepreneurship opportunities.

Key areas of Yegna Gize programming include:

  • Youth employment and transition to work: Supporting young people to access internships, work-based learning, employment opportunities, and other pathways into the labour market.
  • Entrepreneurship and enterprise development: Strengthening entrepreneurial knowledge, business skills, growth mindsets, and access to support for young people interested in starting or growing businesses.
  • Skills and mindset development: Building practical, transferable, entrepreneurial, and employability skills, alongside confidence, aspirations, resilience, and positive attitudes towards work and entrepreneurship.
  • Peer-to-peer and youth support mechanisms: Establishing and strengthening youth groups and peer-support approaches that enable young people to learn from and support one another.
  • Role modelling and mentorship: Connecting young people with role models, mentors, entrepreneurs, and other influential individuals who can provide inspiration, guidance, and practical exposure to different livelihood pathways.
  • School-based engagement: Working with schools, teachers, students, and relevant stakeholders to promote entrepreneurship, creativity, growth mindset, career aspirations, and awareness of economic opportunities.
  • Youth-centred media and social and behavioural change communication (SBC): Using Yegnas established multimedia and storytelling platforms to challenge limiting norms, promote positive attitudes towards work and entrepreneurship, and increase young peoples awareness and uptake of available opportunities.
  • Partnerships and systems strengthening: Working with regional and local government structures, CSOs, private-sector actors, educational institutions, and other stakeholders to strengthen the ecosystem supporting youth economic empowerment.

Girl Effect works with local partners to contextualise and implement interventions according to regional realities and the needs of young people. The programme therefore combines national-level approaches with locally relevant implementation, allowing interventions to respond to the different economic, social, cultural, and institutional contexts across the six regions.

Yegna Gize Programme Impact Study

As the programme progresses, Girl Effect Ethiopia intends to commission an independent Impact Study of Yegna Gize to assess the extent to which the programme has contributed to changes in young peoples knowledge, skills, attitudes, aspirations, behaviours, access to opportunities, and economic outcomes.

The study is expected to generate credible evidence on the effectiveness, relevance, and contribution of Yegna Gize interventions and to identify which approaches are working, for whom, under what conditions, and why. The findings will inform programme learning, adaptation, accountability to stakeholders and donors, and future programming and scale-up decisions.

The selected agency will therefore be expected to develop and implement a rigorous and contextually appropriate study methodology that captures both quantitative and qualitative evidence, where appropriate, and considers the diversity of young people, intervention types, implementation approaches, and regional contexts within Yegna Gize. The study should generate actionable evidence and recommendations that can strengthen the programmes contribution to sustainable youth economic empowerment in Ethiopia.

Girl Effect is looking to engage a qualified agency to recruit, train, and deploy experienced data collectors across the specified geographic scope, and to manage the full data collection cycle, from fieldwork through to data analysis and submission in line with Girl Effect Ethiopias tools, sample design, and quality standards.

Who You Are

The ideal candidate/Agency will:

  • Have demonstrated experience managing field-based data collection for household, community, or individual-level surveys in Ethiopia, ideally on youth, gender, education, livelihoods, or social behaviour change topics.
  • Maintain, or be able to rapidly build, a roster of vetted, experienced enumerators with local language coverage and cultural familiarity across some or all of the six Yegna Gize regions (Tigray, Amhara, Oromia, Sidama, Central Ethiopia, South Ethiopia), including hard-to-reach and pastoralist areas.
  • Have hands-on experience with mobile data collection platforms, particularly SurveyCTO, and the ability to train enumerators on tool use ahead of each deployment.
  • Demonstrate robust field supervision and data quality assurance practices — spot-checks, back-checks/call-backs, and real-time progress monitoring against a sample plan.
  • Have in-house or readily available capacity for data cleaning, processing, and first-level quantitative and/or qualitative analysis, with clear documentation of methods.
  • Be able to mobilize and scale data collection teams on short notice against a recurring, on-call task-order structure, without compromising quality or timeliness.
  • Show a genuine commitment to Girl Effects mission and values, with a demonstrated understanding of child/adolescent safeguarding standards appropriate to research involving youth.
  • Be highly organised, detail-oriented, and able to manage multiple concurrent task orders across different regions.

What You will do 

2.1  Geographic Coverage

Data collection will take place across 6 regions and 60+ woredas, including hard-to-reach and pastoralist areas. Exact woreda-level assignments will be shared with the selected agency alongside each task order, together with the corresponding sample size and tool set.

2.2 Sourcing, Vetting, and Onboarding of Data Collectors

The agency is responsible for building and maintaining a roster of qualified, experienced data collectors who can be deployed against Girl Effect Ethiopias task orders. This includes:

  • Recruiting data collectors with relevant prior experience in household or community-level data collection, ideally on similar topics (e.g., health, gender, youth, social behavior change).
  • Ensuring appropriate local language coverage and cultural familiarity for each assigned region/woreda, including pastoralist communities.
  • Verifying qualifications, references, and prior fieldwork experience before onboarding.
  • Maintaining a sufficient bench of vetted collectors to meet fluctuating task-order demand without delays.
  • Ensuring the data collectors are given a functioning tab and are trained on the use of survey CTO.

2.3 Training

The agency will organize and deliver training for all data collectors before each deployment, covering:

  • Use of Girl Effect Ethiopias data collection tools and mobile data collection platform.
  • The sample design and how it translates into fieldwork assignments.
  • Data quality, ethics, consent, and child/adolescent safeguarding protocols appropriate to the population being surveyed.
  • Logistics, reporting lines, and escalation procedures for field issues.

Girl Effect Ethiopia will provide technical content on the tools and safeguarding standards; the agency is responsible for organizing, scheduling, and delivering the training itself, and for confirming collector competency before deployment (e.g., through a short practical assessment or pilot/pre-test).

title: Ethiopia Innovations and Growth Lead
description:
About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africas farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions.

To learn more, please see our Why Work Here blog post.

One Acre Fund has been working with farmers in the Amhara region of Ethiopia since 2014, with a specific focus on trees since 2018. The Ethiopia program has now expanded into the South Region of Ethiopia in 2024. Our aim with the tree program is to provide not only short-term income opportunities but also long-term benefits, such as soil health improvements and erosion control, so that farmers build resilience over time.

About the Role

The Innovations & Growth Lead will be an essential part of our leadership team in one of One Acre Funds fastest-growing country programs and report directly to the Country Director. 

As an Innovations & Growth Lead, you will sit at the intersection of high-level strategy and "last-mile" delivery, shaping the strategy to plant 100 million trees and generate over $100M additional impact for 440,000 Ethiopian farmers by 2030. You will also pioneer the revenue models that will make our impact self-sustaining.

You will lead a high-performing team of innovators and M&E specialists to turn a 5-year vision into a rigorous Learning Agenda”: designing the field trials, mastering the data, and proving what works before we scale it to 440,000 households. You will ensure that every piece of data collected in the field informs our highest-level strategic decisions. If you are obsessed with evidence-based growth and love solving complex operational puzzles in the field, this is for you!.

Success is measured by your ability to reach OAF Ethiopia’s 2030 objectives. You will:

  • Support our network of 1,000+ nursery managers by improving their production and finding new ways to generate income.
  • Engineer innovative, scalable solutions to maximize income for every farmer reached, unlocking opportunities for youth and women.
  • Secure our seed supply through large-scale adoption of the best varieties and partnerships like the Jimma Research Centre.
  • Define the next frontier and move beyond existing programs to identify "whats next." You will lead the feasibility studies to transition OAF Ethiopia from a traditional NGO model to a revenue-generating organization. You will investigate the regulatory landscape and operational requirements, and research and test the most impactful agricultural practices, products, and services for our farmers.

In a single week, you could present our Learning Agenda to our Steerco, deciding which new programs (like carbon credits or market access) are ready for a pilot and which arent yet viable. You would then work with the Tree innovation team to turn raw avocado trial data into a "Go/No-Go" recommendation for national expansion, before travelling to a remote nursery to troubleshoot a pilot in person, interviewing nursery managers to identify why avocado grafting success rates are lagging, and pivoting the training approach on the spot.

Responsibilities

  • Translate our strategy into action: Lead multi-year impact strategies and translate them into specific field interventions across the organization.
  • Drive the "Learning Agenda": Define annual critical questions. You will decide which new services or products enter our pipeline based on scale and ROI, then set SMART objectives. For example, explore the possibility of adding high-value trees.
  • End-to-End Trial Management:  Design multi-year impact models, oversee the full lifecycle of field trials, empower and coach the impact team to research and implement impactful activities, from hypothesis and budgeting to operational workflows and staff training to translating it into actionable recommendations.
  • Evidence-Based Decision Making: Partner with our Monitoring & Evaluation teams to analyze trial data and drive "Go/No-Go" recommendations for the Country Director. 
  • Champion the professional evolution of your direct reports, providing the coaching and clarity needed to turn high-level organizational vision into rigorous, field-level results.

Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning, and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the general qualifications we look for. For this role specifically, you will have:

  • A proven track record with a minimum of 7 years of experience in managing complex projects or operations, or social enterprise programs in emerging markets, e.g., in agricultural innovation, extension, research & development, marketing, product development, consulting or MEL in agriculture, public health, or education (including 3+ years in one of our countries of operation).
  • Experience identifying strategic gaps and designing "Learning Agendas" - knowing exactly which questions we need to answer through field trials before committing to a national-scale rollout.
  • Field-First Mindset: Significant experience living and working in rural or "last-mile" settings, with a deep understanding of the associated operational challenges.
  • Experimental Design & "Piloting" Mindset: Proven ability to design and execute field trials or pilot programs. You understand how to set up a "test vs. control" environment to see if a new intervention actually drives impact, you understand KPIs and success metrics and you have the judgment to adjust as needed when challenges come.
  • Evaluation Frameworks: Analyze qualitative/quantitative field data, and turn raw results into a "Go/No-Go" recommendation for leadership. A plus if experience working with Monitoring & Evaluation (M&E) teams to design surveys.
  • Experience managing large teams (5-10+ team members) and delivering projects successfully.
  • English required, Amharic preferred. 

Preferred Start Date

As soon as possible

Job Location

On-site in Addis Ababa or Bahir Dar, Ethiopia, with regular visits to our field areas of operations (around 35% of the time).

Benefits

Health insurance, housing, and comprehensive benefits

Eligibility

One Acre Fund can support a work permit for this role. However, nationals of (or those with an extensive professional background and work history in) our countries of operation are preferred.

 

Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @oneacrefund.org address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.

Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.

We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.

description:
What we do
 
The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) works worldwide to provide humanitarian protection and assistance to people affected by conflict and armed violence. We take action in response to emergencies and at the same time promote respect for international humanitarian law. We are an independent and neutral organization, and our mandate stems essentially from the Geneva Conventions of 1949. We work closely with National Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies and with their International Federation in order to ensure a concerted, rational and rapid humanitarian response to the needs of the victims of armed conflict or any other situation of internal violence. We direct and coordinate the international activities conducted in these situations.
 Purpose
 
Language is at the heart of humanitarian action; it enables dialogue, builds trust, and ensures that people affected by conflict can express themselves and be heard.
 
The ICRC Interpreter plays a critical role in enabling this by facilitating accurate and meaningful communication among ICRC delegates, affected populations, authorities, and other stakeholders. Through interpretation in sensitive and complex contexts, including protection activities, visits to detainees, family reunification processes, and dialogue with parties to conflict, the Interpreter ensures that every conversation can take place with clarity, respect, and confidentiality.
 
This is a unique, people-centered role that goes beyond translating words. It requires judgment, cultural awareness, and a deep understanding of the humanitarian principles guiding the ICRC’s work, helping build bridges of understanding where communication can make a real difference.
 Accountabilities & functional responsibilities
 

Oral interpretation: from Amharic, Oromo or Tigrinya to English and vice versa during confidential interviews with people deprived of liberty, ICRC institutional dissemination, ICRC dialogue with authorities, activities to establish the family links which includes delivering Red Cross messages, family tracing and visits to families of detainees.
Written translation: translation of Amharic, Oromo or Tigrinya languages (newspaper articles, correspondence, etc.) into written English.
Analysis and reporting as required: analysis of conditions of detention, security and other matters relating to the ICRC's mandate.
Can be asked to provide support on other protection activities as needed.

 Relationships
 

Externally, interacts with the authorities, representatives of other organizations and beneficiaries, both within and outside places of detention. May be called upon to develop a network of contacts related to operational needs.
Internally, interacts with staff in other departments.

 Required profile and skills
 

Excellent command of English (C1) required
Excellent command of Amharic, Oromo or Tigrinya (C1) required
Proficiency in at least two of the above languages is considered a strong asset.
Proficiency in other ICRC operational languages (English, French, Spanish, Russian, Arabic, Portuguese) is a strong asset.
2 years of professional experience. Previous interpreter or translator experience is an advantage.
Strongly motivated by humanitarian work.
Able to work under pressure in a potentially dangerous environment.
Open-minded and adaptable.
University education/degree in interpretation or translation is an advantage.

 Our operational & field constraints
 

In line with the principle of neutrality, the ICRC does not assign personnel to a country of which they are nationals.
Candidates must be in good health and will have to do a medical check-up prior to departure in the field.
Candidates must possess a driving licence (for manual transmission vehicles).
Candidates must be prepared to accept unaccompanied postings (i.e. no spouse, partner, children or dependents) for the first two missions (minimum 12 months each)  or total of 24 months.

 What we offer
 

Rewarding work in a humanitarian and multicultural environment
A two-week orientation course and other opportunities for further in-house training
Attractive social benefits
Join an ICRC talent pool and be considered for future assignments elsewhere

The ICRC values diversity and is committed to creating an inclusive environment. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates!
 Our values
 
At the ICRC, we value impact, collaboration, respect, and compassion. We seek candidates who demonstrate behaviors based on these shared values. For more information on the ICRC values, please visit this page.
